summary: Viewed through a camera monitor we enter a white room where Neo sits alone until Agent Smith and two other Agents arrive. Smith slaps down a manila file labeled "Anderson, Thomas A." and lays out Neo's two lives: law-abiding software writer versus hacker "Neo, guilty of virtually every computer crime." He offers a deal — wipe the slate clean in exchange for helping capture Morpheus, whom he brands a terrorist. Neo refuses, gives Smith the finger, and demands his phone call. Smith asks what good a phone call is if Neo cannot speak, and Neo's mouth seals shut, his lips melding until "all traces of his mouth are gone." Neo lunges for the door but is restrained. The Agents rip open his shirt; Smith produces a fiber-optic wire tap that animates into an insect/fluke-worm creature which burrows into Neo's navel as Smith tells him he will help them "whether you want to or not."

what_changes.before: A detained suspect still believing he can assert his rights against the Agents.
what_changes.after: Overpowered and physically invaded, his body no longer his own as a device burrows inside him.
what_changes.evidence: I want my phone call! ... Wild with fear, he lunges for the door but the Agents restrain him, holding him in the chair.

what_changes.before: Able to speak and taunt Smith, demanding his phone call.
what_changes.after: Unable to speak as his mouth physically seals shut and disappears.
what_changes.evidence: strangely he begins to feel the muscles in his jaw tighten ... Neo feels his lips grow soft and sticky as they slowly seal shut, melding into each other until all traces of his mouth are gone.

what_changes.before: Defiant, rejecting the deal with contempt.
what_changes.after: Terrified and helpless as the Agents move to force his cooperation.
what_changes.evidence: How about I just give you the finger -- He does. ... Neo struggles helplessly as Smith dangles the wire over his exposed abdomen.

what_changes.before: Attempting a negotiation, presenting himself as reasonable and betting Neo wants to do the right thing.
what_changes.after: Openly coercive, dropping persuasion for physical enforcement of Neo's compliance.
what_changes.evidence: I believe you want to do the right thing. ... You are going to help us, Mr. Anderson, whether you want to or not.

event_hint.one_line: Agents interrogate and then physically violate Neo after he rejects their deal to betray Morpheus.

uncertain: Whether Neo actually has any information the Agents need, or whether the whole overture is intimidation.
What the wire-tap creature does to Neo beyond burrowing inside him.

minds.wants: To convert Neo into an asset against Morpheus — first by persuasion, then, when that fails, by force.
minds.feels: A cold, proprietary contempt. He frames himself as the reasonable party ('I believe you want to do the right thing'), but the removal of the sunglasses is a deliberate reveal of power, not vulnerability; he enjoys the theater of it. When Neo refuses, there is no frustration, only the smooth pivot to coercion — he never lost control because he never needed Neo's consent.
minds.shows: Measured, almost paternal reasonableness, then clinical efficiency once the deal is rejected. He puts his sunglasses back on the moment Neo refuses — re-hiding the 'ice-blue' eyes, signaling the negotiation is over and the machinery is taking over.
minds.basis: He offers a quid pro quo ('wipe the slate clean'), then says 'You disappoint me' when refused, then smiles at Neo's rights-assertion and asks 'what good is a phone call if you are unable to speak?' before the mouth seals. 'You are going to help us, Mr. Anderson, whether you want to or not.'

believes_about.belief: That Neo is a frightened, rational criminal who can be flipped with a clean record and fear, and who will fold once he understands the cost of refusal.
believes_about.wrong_because: He reads Neo as an ordinary suspect whose resistance is negotiable. He cannot yet conceive that Neo is 'The One' — the very thing ev-004 begins to name — so he mistakes the depth of what Neo will become for the pliability of a small-time hacker. His contempt is built on a categorical error he will pay for later.

minds.wants: To hold onto the one lever he thinks he has — his rights, his phone call, his dignity — and to walk out of the room unchanged.
minds.feels: Underneath the bravado, he 'feels himself sinking into a pit of shit' — he knows, from sc-018's ledge and sc-019's capture, that he is out of his depth. The defiance (giving the finger, 'I know my rights') is a performance he is trying to believe in, and it collapses into genuine terror the instant his body stops obeying him.
minds.shows: Swagger and contempt first — the finger, the 'Gestapo crap' — then naked panic as his jaw tightens and his lips seal. The lunging for the door is the performance ending and the animal taking over.
minds.basis: His arc across the scene: 'Yeah. Wow. That sounds like a real good deal' (feigned dismissal), the finger, 'I want my phone call!', then 'the question unnerves Neo,' jaw tightening, lips sealing, 'wild with fear, he lunges for the door,' then 'struggles helplessly' as the creature burrows in.

believes_about.belief: That this is a normal arrest and he is protected by rights and procedure ('Gestapo crap,' 'I want my phone call').
believes_about.wrong_because: The room is not governed by any law he recognizes — his mouth sealing and the organic wire-tap prove it. He is invoking a social contract that does not apply here, and the horror of the scene is exactly the gap between that belief and the reality that his body is not his own.

believes_about.belief: That Smith is a negotiator he can insult and stall, that the 'deal' is a real offer with real refusal rights.
believes_about.wrong_because: Smith's offer was never an offer; 'whether you want to or not' reveals it was always a formality preceding enforcement. Neo mistakes the presentation of choice for the existence of choice.

minds.wants: To witness and enforce — to be the physical certainty behind Smith's words.
minds.feels: Amused, expectant. They were skeptical of Smith's soft approach ('My colleagues believe that I am wasting my time with you') and are gratified when it fails, because it vindicates their instinct that force was always the answer.
minds.shows: They 'snicker' at Neo's confusion turning to panic, then wordlessly restrain him and rip his shirt open on Smith's nod — efficient, silent, physical.
minds.basis: 'The standing Agents snicker, watching Neo's confusion grow into panic.' Smith's earlier line that his colleagues think he's wasting his time. Their restraint of Neo and opening of his shirt on the nod.

believes_about.belief: That he is merely a target to be processed, not a person to be reasoned with.
believes_about.wrong_because: Inferred — their snickering dehumanization treats him as an object to be wired, which is precisely the category error Smith shares and which the coming events (ev-004 onward) will overturn.

connects_back: sc-018: Morpheus's 'two ways out — the scaffold or their custody' — Neo chose (or failed) and is now in 'their custody,' exactly the outcome Morpheus warned against.
sc-019: Trinity watching the capture — the rebellion is now aware Neo is in Agent hands, seeding the later extraction.
sc-017–018: Neo's entire arc of being hunted, losing the phone, losing the ledge — here he loses his body's autonomy, the last of his dwindling control.
The manila file 'Anderson, Thomas A.' confirms the Agents have been watching him since before the cubeicle raid, tying the surveillance of sc-017 to this accounting of 'two lives.'
sets_up: ev-004: Neo waking 'physically intact but psychologically shaken' — the trauma of the mouth-sealing and the burrowing creature is what he carries out of here.

ev-008: Neo discovering his 'grafted ports' in the real world — the wire-tap burrowing into his navel is the in-Matrix image of the real tracking device being implanted, so this scene is the cause of that discovery.

ev-004 onward: The Agents now have a trace inside Neo, which is what makes him findable and thus recoverable by Morpheus's crew — the violation is also, ironically, the thread that leads them back to him.
The failure of Smith's coercion (Neo does not actually give up Morpheus) sets up the rebellion's continued operation and the escalation toward Neo being pursued as 'The One.'
dramatic_function: This scene is the story's hinge from chase-thriller into body-horror and revelation: it strips Neo of the illusion that the world he knows operates on rules he can invoke, and it physically marks him. It converts an abstract 'they're coming for you' into an intimate, irreversible violation, so that his later awakening in the real world (the ports, the pod) lands as the payoff of a debt this scene incurs. It also establishes Smith's fatal contempt, which is the flaw the rest of the story will exploit.
